answer: Acoustic terrain attestation counters Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to multipath reflections in rugged environments. Each node emits a pulse into a canyon and logs the reverberant echo alongside vocal signatures of a native sparrow. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of maintaining distinct physical transceivers at unique spatial coordinates per persona. However, wind gusts and thermal gradients can distort acoustic propagation, falsely rejecting honest agents.
